proposal:
AUDIT (code read, nothing executed). Soundness stands as written: _verify_certificate rebuilds blocks from every dense clause, confines used forms to the block mask, compares all local points and checks every entry of P·L=I. probe() only deletes input clauses and answers UNSAT solely through verified compression plus 2-SAT. Three facts read from the code:
(a) Every clause of the Neon58 quotient has its own support, so every block is a singleton. probe must return no_clauses_removed, and compress_root would skip with all_variables_in_odd_blocks. Both linear tools are blind to any one-clause-per-support family.
(b) step() caches on the raw restricted tuple, not on canon_plus output. Canonically equal children of different parents, and a state re-entered when the branch variable is absent, each rerun refute. This is consistent with the 4/12 repeats.
(c) On a STUCK state, elim runs attempt (all pos×neg resolvents plus quadratic-subsumption canon) for every variable: O(n·m²·w) per state. windows() ignores clauses wider than 5, so for k≥6 the negative clauses generate no IALH windows.

MECHANISM: CERTIFIED TERM-COVER SPLIT (CTS). A cover is a list of consistent, variable-disjoint terms τ1..τr. Its transversals are the clauses choosing one literal from each term. Certificate: each transversal contains a clause of the state F. The at most d transversals without a witness form a defect list M, and each s in M adds the term ¬s.
Lemma 1 (elementary). F ⊨ ∨τi ∨ ∨¬s, so F is satisfiable iff some canon(F|term) is. Proof: an assignment falsifying every τi falsifies one literal per term, hence a whole transversal s. If s has a witness, F is false; otherwise the assignment satisfies ¬s. Binary branching is the case {v},{¬v}. The certificate is monotone: added clauses never invalidate it, unlike a block stabilizer.
Lemma 2 (uniform link gives one child). Suppose every clause touching vars(τ) either contains a literal of every term or equals ¬τi ∪ ρ, with the same remainder set R for each i. Then every child equals canon(F_out ∪ R). The split is then a branch-free block elimination of Σ|τi| variables that shrinks the formula, even though every single-variable DP step grows it.
Discovery (heuristic). Hash each clause minus one literal. For a seed clause, the bucket at each position gives that literal's alternates, and the part is the literal plus its alternates. Verify all Π|τi| ≤ m+d transversals by lookup; accept only if min|τi| ≥ 2. Apply at a STUCK state before binary branching. Children go through the unchanged step(), dedup and prune.

NEON58 (hand trace, conjectural until run). Seeding on a negative quotient clause gives four terms 'pair all-zero', with 16/16 transversals present. Lemma 2 holds, with R the four positive pair-clauses of the other side. There is one distinct child: 8 variables, 4 binary plus 16 negative clauses. In a selection window of that child, every tuple unit-forces the complementary selection clause false, so I predict an empty_table certificate. Independent-test prediction: one split, 4 children, 1 distinct, zero binary branching, 2 IALH calls (12 measured). Controls: deleting one negative clause must still return SAT, through a defect term if that side is split. Adding (a1∨b1) breaks Lemma 2 and should give at most 2 distinct children, still UNSAT.
For k≥6 the child G_k (k binaries plus 2^k negatives) is beyond window 5. The fixture is G_6. My trace of pinned v5: compression skipped, core no_clauses_removed, IALH UNKNOWN (21 windows, 264 tuples, 0 rows). elim then accepts eliminations of 1,3,5,7,9,11 (70→64 clauses, all 64 sign patterns on the even variables), then 2,4,6,8,10 (64→32→16→8→4→empty). That is 11 accepted steps, UNSAT, peak 0.

BIT WORK. With L literal occurrences and width w: detection costs O(L·w·log n) hashing plus O((m+d)·w·log n) per verified seed, and O(m(m+d)·w·log n) over all seeds. Then r canon calls, then the existing IALH and elim cost per distinct state. On T_k everything is polynomial in m=2^{k+1}+k²; elim on G_k is O(m²·log²m) literal operations. In general, total work is D×poly, where D is the number of distinct canonical states reached. Nothing here bounds D.

STRESS TEST (prose). T_6: 24 variables, 164 clauses, pair-contiguous numbering. Conjecture for pinned v5: peak 2, but fact (c) may exhaust the 20 s budget. A timeout there would indicate a total-work problem, not growth. With CTS: 6 children, 1 distinct, equal to the fixture up to renaming.

CANNOT HANDLE. (1) Products over XOR-forms: on the original 20-variable input the parts are not literals, so CTS needs the exact quotient, which is absent in incompatible-basis cases. (2) Non-uniform extras: still sound, but the r children are distinct and overlapping. (3) Pigeonhole: at-most-one clauses give only star covers ({¬p} against all other ¬q), which is ordinary branching plus UP. Its IALH cost is untouched.
missing_theorem:
T1 (elementary; Lean target): Lemmas 1 and 2, including defect terms and monotonicity under added clauses.
C1 (restricted conjecture, hand-traced for k=4 and k=6 only): for every k and every numbering, CTS on T_k yields one distinct child, and pinned elim refutes it in 2k−1 accepted eliminations with O(m²·polylog m) bit work. Falsify with k=3..7 and random renumberings; elim's tie-breaking depends on numbering.
MT (the actual gap): a merging theorem. Covers overlap (an assignment with two all-zero pairs lies in two children), so a split is not a partition. With r ≤ log2 m (exact products with parts ≥2) and depth ≤ n/2, the tree is bounded only by (log m)^{n/2}. Needed: a polynomial-time cover/variable policy π and a polynomial p with D_π(F) ≤ p(|F|), for a syntactically recognisable class strictly larger than uniform-link products. One candidate is to bound distinct children by the number of distinct restrictions E|τi of the non-uniform clauses E, and prove that the bound persists under recursion. For all CNF such a bound would decide SAT in polynomial time; I have no evidence for it and do not conjecture it.
Also missing: an affine-term version of Lemma 1 (terms as cosets on a block, with a local 2^block certificate). It is required whenever exact compression is skipped.
self_attack:
1. Not new mathematics. Lemma 1 is multiway branching on an implied DNF; Lemma 2 is block variable elimination. The contribution is the certificate shape, monotonicity under extras, and the integration point.
2. Discovery sees only literal products reachable by single swaps from a seed. One padded literal per negative clause, strengthened transversals, or more than d missing clauses hide the product. T_k is its best case.
3. Overlapping children can make CTS worse than binary branching when Lemma 2 fails. A budget is a cap, not a theorem.
4. The Neon58 prediction uses quotient numbering inferred from the trusted branch order, not from running compress_root. Window and IALH counts may differ.
5. The fixture's sat/peak prediction rests on a hand trace of elim. A misread tie-break or an unnoticed subsumption would change accepted_dp, and a rejected elimination would leave a STUCK root and peak ≥1. The IALH counts assume SymPy's HNF returns full-rank unimodular results for these tables.
6. The fixture tests a lemma about the pinned DP, not the unimplemented split. Peak 0 there says nothing about T_6 itself.
7. No lower bound is claimed. From memory, Beame–Impagliazzo–Pitassi–Segerlind show formula-caching search can exceed resolution on some formulas, so Haken's pigeonhole bound does not transfer to this solver. No upper bound follows either.
8. Facts (b) and (c) are read from code, not profiled.
mechanism_signature: Certified term-cover split: multiway branching on an implied DNF whose certificate is clause membership of its transversals, with defect terms that keep it SAT-exact. When links are uniform it collapses to a branch-free block elimination. Work invariant: the number of distinct canonical states D, times polynomial per-state cost.
delta_from_prior: 00080 added fresh definition variables (biclique factoring) and hit the elim-reversal hazard. 00079 needed 2^m class-map tables. Fable73 contracts pairs. CTS adds no variables and no quotient map. It removes an entire product side in one certified step, tolerates up to d missing clauses with exact defect terms, and stays valid under arbitrary added clauses. Also new: the singleton-block blindness of both linear tools, the all-variable attempt cost of elim on STUCK states, the overlap (non-partition) obstruction stated as the missing merging theorem, and a fixture that exercises the pinned DP at width 6, beyond the IALH window.
